agency.name: Vermont Department of Labor, Workers' Compensation Division

ttd.basisLabel: Gross average weekly wage before taxes
ttd.rateText: Two-thirds of the employee's average weekly wages (21 V.S.A. § 642(a)(1)), plus $20.00 per week for each dependent child under 21 (§ 642(b)(1)). Maximum = 150% of the average compensation, minimum = 50%, each rounded to the next higher dollar (§ 601(18)-(19)).
ttd.minText: If the employee's average weekly wage is lower than the minimum, TTD is 90% of the average weekly wage (21 V.S.A. § 601(19)).
ttd.periodLabel: July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 (maximum for injuries after June 30, 1986)

waiting.text: TTD is paid during the disability but not including the first three days, the day of the accident counting as the first day unless the employee received full wages for it (21 V.S.A. § 642(a)(1)). The Department states the worker must be disabled from work 4 days or more to obtain TTD.

ttdDuration.text: Payments continue during the disability and end when it ends (21 V.S.A. § 643); the insurer may discontinue on return to work, medical release, maximum medical improvement or non-cooperation by filing a supported Form 27.

ppd.text: After total disability ends, permanent partial impairment is paid at 66 2/3% of the average weekly wage (within the max/min) for a number of weeks equal to the whole-person impairment percentage x 330 weeks, rated under the AMA Guides, Fifth Edition (21 V.S.A. § 648(a)-(b)).

facts.text: TTD is adjusted on the first July 1 after 26 weeks of benefits and every July 1 thereafter so that it keeps the same ratio to the state average weekly wage (21 V.S.A. § 642(a)(3)); the 2026 adjustment multiplier is 1.043%.
The dependent-child allowance is $20.00 per week per child under 21 until July 1, 2028, when the statute sets it back to $10.00 (21 V.S.A. § 642(b)(1)).
The average weekly wage is computed over the 26 weeks before the injury, and earnings from concurrent employers are combined (21 V.S.A. § 650(a)).
Vermont's maximum weekly compensation is set at 150% of the state average compensation (21 V.S.A. § 601(18)), so the 2026-27 maximum ($1,914.00) is three times the minimum ($638.00).
